property.name: yarn.resourcemanager.hostname
property.description: ResourceManager runs on the master container.

property.name: yarn.nodemanager.resource.memory-mb
property.description: Memory each NodeManager may hand out. Two larger values were measured to be too much on the reference host: at 3072 MB and again at 1536 MB per worker the Docker VM (3.5 GB total) started swapping, DataNode IPC calls timed out after 60 s and YARN killed the tasks (exit 137/143). 640 MB per worker - one 256 MB map or one 384 MB reduce - is the third attempt at a size that fits. UNVERIFIED: no cluster ever started under these values, so treat them as a starting point rather than a validated configuration.

property.name: yarn.nodemanager.resource.cpu-vcores
property.description: One slot per worker: at most three concurrent tasks across the cluster. Host CPU is not the constraint (the VM sees 12 cores), memory is, and one slot keeps the resident set of the three task JVMs bounded. Unverified for the same reason as the memory value above.

property.name: yarn.scheduler.maximum-allocation-vcores
property.description: Every container asks for one vcore, so the slot count above is the real limit.

property.name: yarn.scheduler.minimum-allocation-mb
property.description: Smallest container, matching mapreduce.map.memory.mb. A 512 MB minimum silently rounded every map container up to 512 MB, which double-counted against the 640 MB worker.

property.name: yarn.scheduler.maximum-allocation-mb
property.description: Largest container: a reducer over a 10 MB corpus fits in 512 MB.

property.name: yarn.nodemanager.vmem-check-enabled
property.description: Virtual-memory checks are unreliable in containers and abort valid tasks.

property.name: yarn.nodemanager.pmem-check-enabled
property.description: Physical memory is checked, which is the limit that actually matters.

property.name: yarn.nodemanager.env-whitelist
property.description: Propagates the variables the container launch scripts need.

property.name: yarn.log-aggregation-enable
property.description: Keeps container logs retrievable after a task finishes or dies.
